newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico pension funds president criticizes Cardenas.
newsitem.headline: Mexico pension funds president criticizes Cardenas.

text.p: The head of the Mexican Association of Pension Funds (Amafores) on Monday said salaried employees and workers were confused by a left-wing call for a boycott of the new private retirement system.

Amafores President Ralf Peters told radio network Radio Red said Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, the left-wing frontrunner in the race for Mexico City mayor, did not fully understand the law underpinning the soon-to-be launched private system.
"He has generated more confusion again among workers," Peters said.
Cardenas, the candidate for the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) called on Mexicans last Thursday not to join the private pensions system, to be launched on July 1.
Up until now, pension payments have gone to the state-run Mexican Institute for Social Security and a parallel institution for civil servants.
Cardenas urged workers to leave their retirement contributions in the central bank's account for workers unaffiliated with the new private pension schemes.
Peters reaffirmed that all workers have the option to remain in state-run schemes and not join privately operated retirment funds, known as Afores.
Peters said workers selecting to stay in the old system would not lose contributions made to date for their retirement.
Cardenas, who is leading in polls for the July 6 election of the capital, asserts the new system will take over savings of workers without giving them benefits.
He also has warned that workers would eventually be forced to enter a private scheme and pay commissions to banks to run their pensions.
